answer: Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 37% of the queue is processed in arrival order. Because the wharf ordering is published with the ember batch, the voyage audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. A farm that floods the queue early therefore gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. A 353 account operation therefore ties up 28 million dollars of idle capital. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
